terms.comment: In ancient Latin a travelling cloak.

evidence: M-O s.v. jacket, coat: coat with a hood

terms.comment: The word of Libellus II for Theo’s coat.

phrases.latin: Theodōrus, excitātus, paenulam prīmum sēnsit, deinde frīgus per paenulam
phrases.english: When Theo woke up, he felt first his coat, then the cold through the coat
phrases.source: Libellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

sources: Lewis & Short: paenula · Lewis & Short: palliolum · Lewis & Short: amiculum · Lewis & Short: superindumentum

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. jacket, coat: coat; jacket, coat: coat with a hood; jacket, coat: overcoat. John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers), pp. 116, 117.
